_what: The external data records the submission manuscript uses, each as a citable entry with its repository, accession and the committed fetch product every field was copied from. Rendered into the `Data sources` block of fusion-junction-aso-submission-references.md by research/manuscripts/submission_citations.py.
_why: bioRxiv asks authors to cite the laboratory, website and accession numbers for data they use. These records appeared in the manuscript only as bare inline identifiers — GSE28866, AF289510.1, ACH-001519, RRID:CVCL_1238 — with no entry a reader could resolve, so a reader could see WHICH record was used and not WHOSE it is, WHAT it contains, or WHERE it lives.

_provenance.note: EVERY FIELD BELOW IS COPIED FROM A COMMITTED FETCH PRODUCT IN THIS REPOSITORY, named per entry in `copied_from`. No depositor name, title, accession, date, patent number or file name here was written from recollection. Where a field a citation would normally carry was not captured by the fetch that produced the record — a database release version, say — it is ABSENT and the absence is stated in the entry rather than filled from a plausible value.
_provenance.no_new_network_read_was_needed: All six sources had already been retrieved for other parts of this work; this file gives their records a citable home beside the manuscript rather than only inside an analysis artifact.

_what_this_is_not: NOT numbered into the main reference list. That list is generated from the PubMed identifiers carried in the manuscript's superscript comments, and a database record has no PMID; giving one a number would mean inventing an annotation the numbering machinery cannot check. These are cited in the text by accession, which is the citation form the repositories and the Resource Identification Initiative specify, and listed here in full.
NOT a claim that any of these records supports the sentence it is attached to. It is a claim about what the record IS and where it lives.
NOT a re-reading of any of them. The readings stay in the analysis artifacts that own them.

entries.⛔_no_doi_is_asserted: DepMap quarterly releases are distributed through Figshare+ and each carries a DOI, but no fetch in this repository captured one — the inventory read was against the Figshare API's article endpoint, which returned the file list this citation names and which was not stored with its DOI field. A DOI reconstructed from a Figshare article number is a guess, so the article number is given as the hosting location and no DOI is written. This is the correct citation form for a database release: repository, release label, files, accession.

entries.citation: Cellosaurus (SIB Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics). Cell-line records H-EMC-SS (RRID:CVCL_1238), USZ20-EMC1 (RRID:CVCL_C6MX) and USZ22-EMC2 (RRID:CVCL_C6MY). https://www.cellosaurus.org/
entries.used_for: the short tandem repeat profile and the explicit caution on H-EMC-SS, and the curated fusion annotations on the two USZ models, all in §3
entries.⚠_why_this_gets_one_entry_and_not_three: An RRID is designed to be the citation: cited inline it resolves to exactly one record, which is why the Resource Identification Initiative asks authors to write the RRID in the text rather than to add a reference. The three RRIDs in the manuscript are therefore already in correct form and are NOT defective citations. This entry exists for the second thing the manuscript does with them — it READS data out of the records (a STR profile, a caution, two curated fusion annotations) — and that use names a data source a reader should be able to attribute to a laboratory and a website.
entries.⛔_no_release_version_is_asserted: Cellosaurus is versioned and a complete data citation would name the release the records were read from. The two fetches that produced these records did not capture the version field, so none is written. The retrieval is dated in the artifacts named above; the version is absent because it was not read, not because Cellosaurus has none.
